candidates.title: Algo. Riddim: Epic B & Uproot Andy (QUENCH)
candidates.price_text: $5 online (limited), $10 at the door before midnight
candidates.summary: Epic B and Uproot Andy, two long-running NY DJs on the Latin and dancehall circuit, run Algo. Riddim at Friends and Lovers in Crown Heights: dembow, dancehall, afrobeat, amapiano, gqom, reggaeton, kuduro, start to finish. Doors 10pm, goes to 4am, $5 if you buy online and $10 at the door before midnight. No requests.
candidates.fit: This is the Brooklyn Caribbean and West African floor he keeps asking for, run by residents rather than a promoter with a bottle-service model, in a Crown Heights bar he has never been sent. Ten dollars, fifteen minutes from Fort Greene, and the kind of room where you can actually talk to the bartender.

candidates.title: SAZONAO with DJ Woof and Spuddy Roots
candidates.price_text: $5 early-bird online, $10 at the door
candidates.summary: Resident DJ Woof plays reggaeton, afrobeat, dembow, dancehall, pop and cumbia with Spuddy Roots playing live percussion over the top, 10pm until 4am. Friday night at Friends and Lovers in Crown Heights. $5 early-bird online, $10 at the door, no requests.
candidates.fit: Live percussion over a reggaeton and afrobeats set is the Friday version of the diaspora party he wants, and it is a 200-capacity neighborhood bar, not a club with a list. Cheap enough to bring two or three friends without a plan B.

candidates.title: Niche Night NYC presents Y2K Baby: One More Time
candidates.price_text: free, no cover
candidates.summary: A late-90s and early-2000s throwback night: pop, R&B, eurodance and rock throwbacks all evening at Friends and Lovers. Runs 7pm to midnight on a Thursday and there is no cover.
candidates.fit: His Thursday slot, a free door, and the 2000s nostalgia lane that the ABBA night and the Linkin Park and blink ticks point straight at. Starts at 7 and ends at midnight, so it is a dad-compatible night out rather than a 2am set.

candidates.title: John Summit: CTRL ESCAPE Arena Tour with Cassian and Jackie Hollander
candidates.summary: John Summit plays Barclays Center two nights running, Saturday and Sunday of Thanksgiving weekend, with Cassian and Jackie Hollander supporting. Doors-to-stage listed at 7:00PM; 18+ recommended, all ages admitted.
candidates.fit: House headliner in his lane, in the arena he can walk to from Fort Greene, on the weekend his friends are already off work. This is the big-room, a-few-times-a-year pick, and Cassian on the undercard is the melodic end he actually plays at home.

candidates.title: Tyla
candidates.price_text: resale listings were starting around $100 when checked; face value not confirmed
candidates.summary: Tyla plays Brooklyn Paramount at 8pm on Saturday November 28, with a second Brooklyn Paramount date listed for Sunday November 29. The amapiano-pop singer is touring behind her second record; the Paramount is a restored 2,700-seat theater in Downtown Brooklyn.
candidates.fit: The one headliner-level name from his amapiano and Afrobeats phase with an actual New York date in the next six weeks, and she is doing it in a theater a ten-minute walk from his door rather than an arena. Works as a date night as much as a guys' night.

candidates.title: Brent Faiyaz
candidates.time_text: evening, exact set time not confirmed
candidates.summary: Brent Faiyaz headlines Barclays Center on Thursday December 3. It is the only hip-hop-adjacent arena booking at Barclays inside the radar window besides John Summit.
candidates.fit: Thursday is his night and Barclays is a walk from Fort Greene. Faiyaz sits right next to the Don Toliver and Gunna end of his library, so it is the hip-hop lane covered without a trip to Manhattan.

candidates.title: R&B Only Live
candidates.summary: The touring R&B Only singalong party takes over Brooklyn Paramount on Saturday January 2. It is a DJ-led, crowd-singing format built on 2000s and 2010s R&B rather than a concert.
candidates.fit: Same register as the ABBA night he dressed up for and the emo-night lane: everybody knows every word, nobody is watching a DJ's laptop. First Saturday of the new year, a walk from home, and it needs booking now because the room is 2,700 seats.

candidates.title: Afrobeat Nights NYC (Fall Series)
candidates.summary: Afrobeat Nights brings amapiano and Afrobeats to the 280-capacity Sultan Room in Bushwick for its fall series, doors at 11pm and running to 4am, 21+. Listings disagree slightly on whether this one is billed as the Saturday night or the Sunday morning date, so confirm on Dice before buying.
candidates.fit: A 280-cap room is exactly his size, and the Sultan Room is a Bushwick venue the email has never sent him. The caveat is the hour: this one peaks at 1am, so it is a sometimes thing.

candidates.title: Elsewhere New Year's Eve with San Pacho
candidates.price_text: from $55
candidates.summary: Elsewhere's New Year's Eve is headlined by San Pacho, the Colombian-Dutch house producer, with the rest of the lineup still TBA. Listings show a 9pm start, 21+, tickets from $55.
candidates.fit: If the Paramount reggae NYE is too dressy, this is the house-music version in a Bushwick room with a rooftop, at a price that does not involve a table minimum. Lineup is incomplete, so treat it as a hold rather than a lock.

candidates.title: Snakehips (DJ set) with L3Ni and TWOFACED
candidates.summary: Snakehips headline Elsewhere on Saturday November 21 with L3Ni and TWOFACED, plus a separate aNYthing Goes room. Elsewhere is a multi-room Bushwick club; the exact room and door time were not confirmed.
candidates.fit: A name he would recognize from the 2016-era festival end of his library, playing a club room rather than a festival stage. Second-tier pick this week behind the Crown Heights parties, since Elsewhere is a room he has already been sent.

candidates.title: Friends & Lovers Open Jam
candidates.price_text: free entry, one drink minimum to play
candidates.summary: An open jam hosted by local musicians at Friends and Lovers: anyone can get on the mic or an instrument, everyone else watches. Free entry, one drink minimum if you play, 8pm to midnight.
candidates.fit: It lands on the night before Thanksgiving, the biggest bar night of the year, and it is the interactive format he likes rather than standing and watching. Free, Crown Heights, home by one.

candidates.title: Other Half Stout Season Festival 2026
candidates.price_text: ticketed on Eventbrite, price not confirmed
candidates.summary: Other Half's annual Stout Season Festival returns on December 5, 2026 at their original Centre Street brewery in Brooklyn, with unlimited stout pours from more than 40 visiting breweries. Tickets are on sale now through Eventbrite. The date, venue and format are stated on Other Half's own site; I could not open the Eventbrite page to read session times or the ticket price.
candidates.fit: He ticked brewery events as 'keep it coming' and Strong Rope on a sunny day is a standing favorite, but this is the winter version: a pour-fest built for three or four guys with a stated end time, in his own half of Brooklyn, not another DJ in a warehouse.

candidates.title: MŪJE x TIN's one-night collaboration dinner
candidates.summary: MŪJE, the contemporary Asian restaurant from Jungsik Yim, hosts TIN's for a single-night collaboration dinner on Monday November 16, with executive chefs Daeik Kim and Justin Choung reworking MŪJE's eight-course tasting menu around TIN's Shanghainese signatures: sheng jian bao with truffle, Lah Nyo scallion noodles. TIN's built a new tableside cocktail pairing for it, including a rum milk punch with chili crisp oil. Two seatings, 5pm and 8pm; I could not reach a booking page, so the price per head is unconfirmed.
candidates.fit: This is exactly the restaurant-in-restaurant format he asked for, and it is the first night of a new collaboration series at MŪJE, which means the next ones are worth watching. Caveat for him: it is a Monday in NoMad, so it only clears his bar as a date-night splurge, not a group plan.

candidates.title: Maccabee Bar, the Hanukkah pop-up
candidates.summary: Naomi Levy's Hanukkah pop-up takes over a host bar each December with themed cocktails, latkes and full Hanukkah decor; past New York editions have run in the West Village. Hanukkah 2026 falls December 4 through December 12. I read the Maccabee Bar homepage, which points to a 'this year's pop-ups' locations page, but my fetch budget ran out before I could open it, so the 2026 host bar and opening date are unconfirmed.
candidates.fit: He has already done a Hanukkah-themed cocktail bar and loved it, and the Jewish-culture lane is one he ticked repeatedly, so this is the one seasonal bar worth having on the radar before it fills up. Treat it as a lead to confirm, not a booked plan.

candidates.title: The Collectors Bar
candidates.summary: A Hong Kong-inspired cocktail bar and speakeasy that opened on Grand Street in Brooklyn in early 2026, per Greenpointers. I only have the publication's headline from a search result; I could not open the article or the bar's own page, so hours, exact address and the drinks program are unconfirmed.
candidates.fit: He collects hidden bars the way other people collect restaurants, and this is a 2026 opening in the Williamsburg orbit he already trains in, not another Manhattan speakeasy everyone has sent him. Verify the address before he walks over.

candidates.title: Tristan & Yseult (Emma Rice / Wise Children)
candidates.time_text: evening curtains most nights, matinees on the weekend; runs about 2 hours 10 minutes with no listed intermission
candidates.price_text: from $49
candidates.summary: Emma Rice's company brings her long-touring Tristan & Yseult back to St. Ann's Warehouse for a run that ends Sunday Nov 22. It is the Arthurian love story played as a live-band variety show: brass, pop songs, anoraks, audience in the thick of it. Tickets start at $49 and the run time is about 2h10.
candidates.fit: This is the Dumbo room ten minutes from Fort Greene that the email has used once and then forgotten, and it is the opposite of generic theater: a live band, jokes, spectacle, a company that tours the world. Closing weekend gives him a reason to book the sitter now rather than later.

candidates.title: Lightscape 2026 opening weekend
candidates.time_text: after dark, timed entry slots through the evening; the trail is about a mile and takes roughly an hour
candidates.price_text: peak entry $44 adults, $28 children; Anytime Entry $59; under 2 free
candidates.summary: Lightscape, the Botanic Garden's illuminated winter trail, opens Friday Nov 20 and runs through Jan 3. Sixth year, roughly a mile of installations and over a million lights, timed entry. Peak tickets are $44 adult and $28 child, with $59 Anytime Entry if he wants flexibility.
candidates.fit: He already lists the Botanic Garden light show as one of the best things he has done in the city, and opening weekend is the one time it is not wall-to-wall. Carrier-friendly for the 1-year-old early in the evening, and it doubles as a short date night if they go without him.

candidates.title: Nutcracker Rouge
candidates.time_text: evening shows Wednesday through Sunday, plus late weekend seatings; arrive early for the lounge
candidates.price_text: from about $35 Thursday, $39 Friday; premium seats and banquettes cost considerably more
candidates.summary: Company XIV's baroque-burlesque Nutcracker is open at Théâtre XIV in Bushwick and runs into late January. Circus, opera, dance and striptease in a 150-ish seat cabaret room with its own cocktail bar. Thursday seats were listed from $35 and Friday from $39 via TodayTix.
candidates.fit: His favorite theater company in the city, and the Halloween show was a highlight, so this is the one Company XIV pick of the stretch rather than a weekly habit. Book a Thursday if he wants it cheaper and quieter than the holiday-season weekends.

candidates.title: SAIGON
candidates.time_text: evening performances with weekend matinees; this is a long one, check run time before booking the sitter
candidates.price_text: not confirmed; St. Ann's tickets generally start around $49
candidates.summary: St. Ann's second winter production, SAIGON, plays Dec 3 to 20. It is the big international import of their season, staged in the Tobacco Warehouse space in Dumbo. Dates confirmed by TodayTix; prices and curtain times were not posted where I could read them.
candidates.fit: The ambitious-international-company slot at St. Ann's is exactly the front-yard programming the email keeps skipping, and a December date night that is not a Christmas market or a light trail. Three weeks only, so it needs booking in November.

candidates.title: Duncan Trussell
candidates.summary: Duncan Trussell, the Duncan Trussell Family Hour host and co-creator of Netflix's The Midnight Gospel, plays the Bell House on Wednesday Nov 18 at 7:30pm. The venue calendar confirms date and time; price was not shown.
candidates.fit: Podcast-famous name, 500-cap room, ten minutes from Fort Greene. Midweek, so only worth it if the guys want something low-stakes that is not a bar.

candidates.title: Meat Cats Comedy Presents: Saturday Sauce
candidates.price_text: not confirmed; Union Hall late shows generally run $15 to $20
candidates.summary: Union Hall's late Saturday stand-up showcase stacks eight comics — Britt Migs, Irina Chelidze, Chloe Radcliffe, James Mwaura, Carolina Montesquieu, Joe Palana, Max Higgins and Clare Donaher — into the downstairs room at 10pm. That room is a 100-capacity basement with bocce courts and a bar upstairs.
candidates.fit: A hundred seats, drinks upstairs first, and eight shots at a comic worth remembering: the right shape for a three-guy Saturday that does not commit the whole night. No name on the bill he would know, so this is the backup rather than the headline.

candidates.title: ARTOON NETWORK: The Cartoon Art Show NYC
candidates.price_text: not confirmed; ticketed on Eventbrite
candidates.summary: A travelling cartoon-art show takes over The Tiny Cupboard's comedy club and game bar in Bushwick on Saturday Nov 21, 7 to 10pm. It is an art opening in a room with a bar, arcade games and a rooftop, not a white-cube gallery.
candidates.fit: He liked his wife's friend's photo studio party better than most club nights; this is that register — an opening that is actually a party, in a Bushwick room the email has never sent him to. Easy to pair with a late comedy set in the same building.

candidates.title: Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire, Entirely From Memory
candidates.price_text: not confirmed; Littlefield comedy generally $18 to $25
candidates.summary: Thursday Nov 19 at 8pm, Littlefield hosts a live recounting of Goblet of Fire performed entirely from memory — one of the cult comedy formats where the joke is the recall, not the film. Gowanus, bar in the room, roughly 200 standing.
candidates.fit: A format the email has never sent him, on his main weeknight, a ten-minute car ride away. Flagged honestly: Littlefield has carried picks three times already, so this only wins if the Thursday alternative is another DJ.

candidates.title: Red Bastard at Brooklyn Comedy Collective
candidates.time_text: evening; exact night and curtain need confirming on the BCC schedule
candidates.price_text: not confirmed
candidates.summary: Brooklyn Comedy Collective's November schedule lists Red Bastard, the cult bouffon show in which a performer in a grotesque inflated suit bullies, flirts with and interrogates the audience for an hour. BCC runs out of Eris on Graham Avenue, a basement room well under 100 people. The exact performance night inside this week was ambiguous on the listing I could read.
candidates.fit: Interactive in the way he actually means it — he gets talked to, argued with and put on the spot, not just watched — and it is as far from a DJ booth as this lane gets. Confirm the night before he texts anyone.

candidates.title: George Balanchine's The Nutcracker, New York City Ballet
candidates.time_text: evening and matinee performances daily through the holidays
candidates.address: 20 Lincoln Center Plaza, New York, NY 10023
candidates.price_text: not confirmed this week; NYCB Nutcracker seats typically run from the low $40s to well over $200
candidates.summary: New York City Ballet's Nutcracker opens the day after Thanksgiving and runs through the holidays at the Koch Theater. The opening date was carried on NYCB's own site as 'Nutcracker opens Nov 27'; I could not re-read the calendar this week for the closing date, exact curtains or current price bands.
candidates.fit: He has called this his favorite night in the city. The only useful thing the email can do is tell him in November that the good Saturday evenings go first — if he wants a specific date with his wife, buy it this week.

candidates.title: Brooklyn Museum First Saturday, December
candidates.time_text: evening, typically 5pm to 10pm, free entry with timed tickets released in advance
candidates.price_text: free, timed tickets
candidates.summary: The museum's monthly free Saturday night — DJs, dancing in the Beaux-Arts Court, talks and open galleries — falls on Dec 5. The December program had not been confirmed by me this week; the lineup usually posts about two weeks out.
candidates.fit: A free party in a landmark building fifteen minutes from his door, with a real crowd rather than a listicle crowd, and it is the rare thing that works whether he brings the guys or his wife. Check the posted program before committing.

candidates.title: Lil' Kim: Hard Core Symphony with the Illharmonic Orchestra
candidates.summary: Lil' Kim performs her 1996 debut Hard Core plus her hits with the Illharmonic Orchestra doing live orchestral arrangements, at the restored 3,000-seat Kings Theatre in Flatbush. Wednesday Nov 18 at 8pm is still on sale at $157 to $365; the second night, Thursday Nov 19, is listed sold out.
candidates.fit: His 2000s New York rap streak (Dipset, Styles P, Big Pun) meets a format he has never been sent: a Brooklyn rap institution with a full orchestra behind her, ten minutes down Flatbush from Fort Greene. Wednesday is normally off-limits for him, which is the one catch, but the Thursday is gone.

candidates.title: A Very Good Night of Comedy: Jerry Seinfeld, Louis C.K., Leanne Morgan, Marcello Hernández, George Wallace
candidates.summary: A one-night stacked stand-up bill at the 2,900-seat Beacon with Jerry Seinfeld, Louis C.K., Leanne Morgan, SNL's Marcello Hernández and George Wallace. Doors and ticket prices were not confirmed on the organizer page; the listing is Tuesday Nov 17 at 7:30pm.
candidates.fit: Five headliners on one bill, including a current SNL cast member, is the 'names in town' event of the week even if the room is bigger than his sweet spot; it is a Tuesday, so it only clears his bar because of who is on it.

candidates.title: Stevie Wonder: Songs in the Key of Life 50th Anniversary
candidates.summary: Stevie Wonder plays Songs in the Key of Life in full for the album's 50th anniversary at Madison Square Garden on Thursday Nov 19 at 8pm. Ticket prices were not listed on the aggregator page I read.
candidates.fit: The big-spectacle-a-few-times-a-year slot, on his main weeknight: his library runs deep on Bill Withers, Nat King Cole and classic soul, and a full-album Stevie Wonder night is the kind of thing his wife will remember like the Nutcracker.

candidates.title: The 46th Annual John Lennon Tribute (benefit for Theatre Within)
candidates.summary: The long-running annual John Lennon tribute concert, a benefit for Theatre Within, takes over the 1,500-seat Town Hall on Saturday Nov 21 at 8pm. The bill rotates every year and the full lineup was not on the listing page I read.
candidates.fit: Beatles tracks are all over his library and this is a 46-year-old New York tradition in a 1,500-seat room rather than a nostalgia arena show, which is the register he actually likes for a Saturday with his wife.

candidates.title: VEENA.NYC presents IN IMPROVISATION ft. Heems, Lee Ranaldo, Hisham Bharoocha & more
candidates.price_text: about $29, 21+
candidates.summary: A one-off improvisation session with Heems (Das Racist), Lee Ranaldo of Sonic Youth, Hisham Bharoocha and others in the roughly 200-capacity Sultan Room in Bushwick, Friday Nov 20 at 8pm, around $29, 21+.
candidates.fit: This is the shape he keeps asking for: people whose records he knows, in a room of 200, doing something that only exists for one night, for the price of two drinks. Bushwick on a Friday, no tourist energy.

candidates.title: Gianmarco Soresi: The Silver Lining
candidates.summary: Gianmarco Soresi, whose crowd-work clips have made him one of the bigger touring names to come out of the New York clubs, headlines the Bell House on Sunday Nov 29. Date confirmed on the venue calendar; price not listed.
candidates.fit: Thanksgiving-weekend Sunday, a 500-person room, and a comic whose crowd work means the night is different depending on who is in the seats, which suits his taste for shows he is part of rather than watching.

candidates.title: Jacqueline Novak
candidates.summary: Jacqueline Novak, of the Netflix special Get On Your Knees, plays the Bell House on Monday Nov 23. The venue calendar marks the show SOLD OUT.
candidates.fit: Radar only: a Netflix-special name in a 500-cap room is exactly the trade he likes, but it is already gone, so it is a watch-for-a-release or resale situation rather than a plan.

candidates.title: Jaboukie Young-White
candidates.summary: Daily Show correspondent and Rap Sh!t writer Jaboukie Young-White headlines the Bell House, roughly 500 capacity, on Tuesday Nov 17 at 7:30pm. Price was not listed on the venue page.
candidates.fit: A face he knows from TV doing a full hour in a Gowanus ballroom rather than a theater; it is a Tuesday, so it is a 'if the babysitter is free anyway' pick rather than the lead.

candidates.title: Danny Brown
candidates.summary: Danny Brown headlines the 1,200-capacity Irving Plaza on Thursday Nov 19 at 7pm. Ticket price was not listed on the aggregator page I read.
candidates.fit: A rapper with a decade of festival headline slots playing a 1,200-room on his main night out; it is the smallest room Danny Brown plays in this city, which is the whole point of this lane.

candidates.title: DOC NYC: You Can See Everything (Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim)

The festival page lists this screening as rush only, and the directors' Q&A was attached to the film's first festival screening, which has already happened.
candidates.fit: Fielder is a ticked name and this is the film everyone will be arguing about by Christmas; the heads-up is that the Q&A screening is gone and this is a rush line at 3pm on a Tuesday, so it is only realistic if he can duck out of work.

candidates.title: Stamptown
candidates.summary: The touring Stamptown comedy variety show lands at the Bell House on Monday Nov 30. The venue calendar confirms the date; lineup and price were not published on the page I read.
candidates.fit: Stamptown is a rotating variety bill that regularly drops in names without announcing them, which is the closest thing to the surprise-drop-in format he likes; Monday night is the catch, and the lineup needs checking before it is worth a text to the guys.

candidates.title: A Drinking Game NYC: The Muppet Christmas Carol
candidates.summary: A Drinking Game NYC stages a live, audience-participation script reading of The Muppet Christmas Carol with comedians and actors at the Bell House on Friday Dec 11. Date and venue confirmed on the Bell House calendar; price was not listed.
candidates.fit: Interactive, holiday, and a bar room rather than a theater, which is the bucket he keeps saying yes to (punk trivia, bingo, costume screenings) and a Friday he can actually use.

candidates.title: How Nick Stole Christmas: A Christmas Comedy Cabaret
candidates.summary: A holiday comedy cabaret at the Bell House on Tuesday Dec 15 at 7:30pm, confirmed on the venue's own calendar. Lineup and price were not published on the page I read.
candidates.fit: Filed for the holiday-traditions-with-friends lane he ticks automatically every December; it is a Tuesday, so it only matters if the bill turns out to carry a name worth the babysitter.

candidates.title: Tammam Azzam: A New York Debut — artist talk with curator Saria AlMidani (exhibition "A Horizon Remains" on view through Dec 3)
candidates.time_text: talk 6:30pm to 8:30pm; the exhibition is open during institute hours
candidates.price_text: not listed on the Eventbrite snippet; Goethe-Institut talks are usually free with RSVP
candidates.summary: Syrian artist Tammam Azzam, based in Germany, has his first New York solo show at the Goethe-Institut; on Tuesday Nov 17 he sits down with curator Saria AlMidani to talk about the work. The painting show, A Horizon Remains, stays up at 30 Irving Place through December 3, so the room is walk-in-able any weekday after the talk.
candidates.fit: German-institute programming is his lane and this is a small room, not a museum crowd — but be straight with him: last week's email already carried this talk, so the only new thing here is the exhibition itself as a free 20-minute stop. Lead with something else.

candidates.title: Catherine Malabou: The Afterlife of Sacrifice — Bataille after Agamben
candidates.price_text: free, RSVP required
candidates.summary: Deutsches Haus at NYU hosts French philosopher Catherine Malabou for an in-person lecture in their townhouse on Washington Mews on Wednesday Dec 2 at 5:30pm. Deutsches Haus events are free and open to the public, with limited space, so RSVP.
candidates.fit: It is the German-institution lane he asked for and the room is tiny, but it is a philosophy lecture on a Wednesday — that is his 'only if exceptional' slot. Send it as radar, not a main pick, unless the rest of the December German calendar stays empty.

candidates.title: Pearls of Yiddish Song Live / Riki Rose in concert (National Yiddish Theatre Folksbiene)
candidates.price_text: not confirmed
candidates.summary: Folksbiene's season-111 brochure lists a December 29, 2026 7pm concert at Drom on Avenue A — a Yiddish-music night built around Riki Rose, the Williamsburg-raised Yiddish rock singer, in the Pearls of Yiddish Song live series. Drom is a 200-ish-capacity room, not a theater.
candidates.fit: Yiddish music in a small club rather than a museum auditorium is exactly the Jewish-culture register he keeps not getting, and it is the kind of room where he can stand at the bar. Do not send it until someone confirms the date and ticket link — the brochure line is all I could read.

candidates.title: Rock and Roll Playhouse — Sunday morning kids' concert
candidates.price_text: typically around $20 a ticket, under 1 free

candidates.title: Governors Island ferry morning

candidates.price_text: ferry a few dollars round trip; free before noon on weekends in past seasons

candidates.fit: He ticked Governors Island and the Rockaway ferry on the checklist, and a boat with a destination is the family format he keeps liking. Verify the November ferry times on govisland.com before you commit a Saturday to it.

candidates.title: Brooklyn Children's Museum weekend programming
candidates.price_text: ticketed; check the site
candidates.summary: The Crown Heights museum runs scheduled weekend workshops and performances on top of general admission, and the under-two areas are separate from the big-kid floors. It is a fifteen-minute drive from Fort Greene.
candidates.fit: A rainy-Saturday fallback in a neighborhood he already likes, and close enough to the Jewish Children's Museum up the road that he could pair them. Nothing here is confirmed for a specific date — pull the weekend's program list before sending.

candidates.title: LCD Soundsystem at Music Hall of Williamsburg

candidates.fit: This is the exact shape of the pick he says the email keeps missing: a band everyone knows crammed into a 650-cap room he trains ten minutes from, announced four days out. Tuesday is normally a no, but this is the 'exceptional' case.

candidates.title: STING 3.0 at Brooklyn Paramount
candidates.summary: Sting is in the middle of a multi-night STING 3.0 stand at the restored Brooklyn Paramount, a roughly 2,700-cap room, with Ticketmaster listing a Saturday Nov 21 7pm date (and a Tuesday Nov 17). The venue posted on Nov 16 that four nights remain. Prices vary by night and were not confirmed.
candidates.fit: Dad-rock-adjacent arena name playing a theater he can walk to from Fort Greene, on a Saturday night. Big enough to be a plan, small enough that it isn't a Barclays slog.

candidates.summary: Bridget Everett (Somebody Somewhere) plays four previously sold-out nights at Joe's Pub with her band The Tender Moments, Nov 17 through Nov 20, doors 9pm. Joe's Pub released a limited batch of additional tickets this week. Tickets are $85 to $135 with a two-drink minimum.
candidates.fit: A face he'd recognize from HBO doing filthy, loud cabaret in a 180-seat room; Thursday or Friday works, and it is more interesting than another burlesque run for a babysitter night.

candidates.title: Family Concert: The Pop Ups + Princess Backpack and Benjamin
candidates.price_text: $24 adult, free for kids 18 and under, includes museum admission
candidates.summary: The Grammy-nominated kids' band The Pop Ups share a Sunday morning bill with Princess Backpack and Benjamin in the Jewish Museum's Scheuer Auditorium, 11:30am to 12:30pm on Nov 22. Tickets are $24 for adults, free for children, and include museum admission. Reservations required for adults and kids both.
candidates.fit: A real band in a real auditorium rather than a playground, done by 12:30, and it sits in the Jewish-culture lane he ticked with the Jewish Children's Museum.

candidates.title: TV on the Radio: the final two nights of Music Hall of Williamsburg
candidates.summary: TV on the Radio will play the last two nights ever at Music Hall of Williamsburg on Dec 5 and 6 before the venue closes. Presale registration is open now, the presale runs Thu Nov 19 noon to 10pm, general on sale is Fri Nov 20 at noon, and a limited number of tickets go on sale in person at the box office Sat Nov 21, 12pm to 6pm.
candidates.fit: Book-now radar: a Brooklyn band closing a Brooklyn room for good is a story he'll want to have been at, and the in-person box office window on Saturday is the kind of detail that gets you in when the on-sale melts.

candidates.title: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring, 25th anniversary on 35mm
candidates.summary: Nitehawk Prospect Park screens the theatrical cut of Fellowship on 35mm at brunch on Sat Nov 21 and Sun Nov 22, with a repeat at Nitehawk Williamsburg on Monday Nov 30. The cinema posted on Nov 15 that seats are nearly gone. Food and drink service at your seat, as always at Nitehawk.
candidates.fit: He ticked Nitehawk themed screenings, and a three-hour 35mm print with brunch is a weekend-daytime plan for the guys that doesn't require a babysitter past bedtime.

candidates.title: Variety Show Bingo at The Tiny Cupboard
candidates.summary: Drag performer Cunning Stunt King hosts another edition of Variety Show Bingo at The Tiny Cupboard on Thursday Nov 19, 6:30 to 8:30pm, with a Taipei drag guest, a birthday-themed open set and a first-time stand-up spot. It runs in a tiny bar room off the Chauncey J, and the only listing is the host's own Instagram post.
candidates.fit: Bar doing weird programming, under 50 people, drag plus bingo plus an open set, and it's done by 8:30 so a Thursday still works for a dad. Nobody in his group chat has heard of it.

candidates.title: Ruth Rehmann's ILLUSIONS: Rob Madole and Megan Nolan at Goethe-Institut
candidates.price_text: free with registration
candidates.summary: Berlin-based translator Rob Madole and novelist Megan Nolan discuss Ruth Rehmann's 1950s West German office novel Illusions, newly back in print via Faber Editions, at Goethe-Institut New York on Thursday Nov 19 at 6:30pm. Free with registration, books for sale and signing afterward.
candidates.fit: German lane, free, Thursday, and a 60-person room rather than a lecture hall. Pairs with dinner nearby if he brings his wife.

candidates.title: Taina Enikeyi at Elsewhere Zone One
candidates.price_text: free with RSVP
candidates.summary: Elsewhere just announced Taina Enikeyi for Saturday Nov 21 in the small room, free with RSVP, billed as world, latin club and afrobeats. Announced only on the venue's Instagram; set times were not posted.
candidates.fit: Afrobeats is his current phase and this is the free, small-room version of it rather than a 2am warehouse. Worth an RSVP even if it's a second stop after dinner.

candidates.title: Tristan & Yseult at St. Ann's Warehouse
candidates.summary: Emma Rice's Tristan & Yseult, the Kneehigh-style version of the love story with a live band and an audience-facing 'Club of the Unloved,' plays its final week at St. Ann's Warehouse through Nov 22. The venue posted on Nov 12 that 13 performances remained. There is a love-notes table in the lobby where the audience writes their own missed connections.
candidates.fit: Theatrical nightlife rather than generic theater, fifteen minutes from his door, and the audience participation element is the kind of thing he actually likes. Closes Sunday, so it's this week or never.

candidates.title: Project 91: The Golden Age of EDM at Le Poisson Rouge
candidates.summary: Project 91 takes over LPR on Friday Dec 18 for a night built entirely on 2010s big-room EDM: Avicii, Swedish House Mafia, Calvin Harris, Hardwell. Tickets via the promoter's link; door price not posted in the announcement.
candidates.fit: His 2016-era festival EDM library is real and the email has never sent him a night of it. A 700-cap basement playing Swedish House Mafia with three friends beats a deep-cut DJ in a good room.

candidates.title: Ayad Akhtar and Daniel Kehlmann on AI and authorship
candidates.summary: Goethe-Institut and PEN America host Pulitzer winner Ayad Akhtar and German novelist Daniel Kehlmann (Measuring the World, Tyll) in conversation about what AI does to authorship, Tuesday Dec 1 at 7pm, $10, reception after.
candidates.fit: German heavyweight in a small Irving Place room for ten dollars, and the subject is closer to his ideas lane than another book reading. Tuesday, so only if the lineup lands for him.

candidates.title: Maccabee Bar, the Hanukkah pop-up, returns to NYC
candidates.summary: Maccabee Bar announced on Nov 8 that NYC reservations are live, released on a rolling 30-day basis, with walk-ins welcome; the Boston edition runs Nov 27 to Dec 31. The NYC host venue and exact run dates were not stated in the post and I could not confirm them this week (past years it has taken over Ollie in the West Village and Saint Tuesday).
candidates.fit: He already loved the Hanukkah cocktail bar once; this is the booking reminder, and the rolling 30-day release means the good December nights go the moment they open.

candidates.title: The Sloppy Boys at littlefield
candidates.summary: The Sloppy Boys, the cocktail podcast and live band from the Birthday Boys trio, play littlefield on Dec 30 as part of a three-city run between Boston and Philadelphia. Tickets are on sale now via the band's link.
candidates.fit: Comedy Bang Bang orbit, a band that drinks its way through the set, in a 250-cap Gowanus room during the dead week between Christmas and New Year when nobody has a plan.

candidates.title: A Christmas Carol & Nightmare Before Christmas Entirely From Memory
candidates.summary: The Entirely From Memory crew puts comedians on stage to recreate two holiday films with no scripts and no rehearsal, at littlefield on Thursday Dec 17. Tickets through the show's link in bio.
candidates.fit: A format he has never been sent: not stand-up, not improv, just comedians butchering films live on a Thursday. Holiday-adjacent without being corny.

candidates.title: Smart Girl Dumb Questions live with Esther Perel at the Comedy Cellar
candidates.summary: Esther Perel joins Nayeema Raza for a live taping of the Smart Girl Dumb Questions podcast at the Comedy Cellar on Monday Nov 30. Tickets via the show's link; price not posted in the announcement.
candidates.fit: He ticked live podcasts with names on stage, and a therapist people actually quote doing it in the Cellar's basement is a stranger room than Town Hall. Monday, so it's a 'only if he's into it' pick.

candidates.title: Son Lux at Pioneer Works
candidates.summary: Son Lux, the trio that scored Everything Everywhere All at Once and Thunderbolts, play the Pioneer Works Main Hall on Dec 18 and 19 alongside a video installation, celebrating their new album Out Into. Openers are mmeadows and Vines on the 18th, Samora Pinderhughes and Holland Andrews on the 19th.
candidates.fit: A credit he knows (that Oscar-winning score) playing a Red Hook industrial hall with projections, which is a better date night than a standard club booking.

candidates.title: Jenny Hagel and Alex Kumin work out new jokes at Union Hall
candidates.summary: Late Night writer and performer Jenny Hagel and Alex Kumin are trying out new material at Union Hall on Dec 6 and Dec 13 with a stacked guest lineup each night, tickets via their link in bio.
candidates.fit: Writers from the SNL/Late Night orbit testing unfinished jokes in a 180-seat basement is the small-room version of the comedy he ticks, and it's a twenty-minute walk from Fort Greene.

candidates.title: Best Year Ever: 30 comedians, best joke of the year
candidates.summary: Thirty comedians each do their single best joke of the year at Union Hall on New Year's Eve at 7:30pm, announced by host Jenny Cestquoi on Nov 16. Tickets via Union Hall.
candidates.fit: A New Year's Eve plan that starts at 7:30 and leaves him home before the babysitter's patience runs out, with thirty punchlines instead of a $200 open bar.

candidates.title: Omnium Circus: I'mPossible Holiday Wonders at BAM
candidates.summary: Omnium Circus makes its BAM debut Dec 11 to 13 with a holiday show of aerial acts, stunts and live music performed by a multi-abled cast, built to be accessible for all audiences. Tickets through BAM.
candidates.fit: The family pick that is actually in his front yard: circus spectacle a toddler can watch from a lap, at the theater he walks past every day and the email has barely used.

candidates.title: Greenlight Bookstore late-night holiday shopping and the FAB Fulton Stroll
candidates.time_text: daytime stroll, plus a ticketed 10pm after-hours session
candidates.summary: Greenlight joins the FAB Fulton Holiday Stroll on Dec 12 with free gift wrapping and seasonal treats, then keeps the doors open at 10pm for a small ticketed group of shoppers. Tickets via the store's link in bio.
candidates.fit: His block, his bookstore, and a version of holiday shopping that is actually a night out for a small group. The email has sent him to Greenlight approximately never.

candidates.title: Bushwick Figure Drawing: pirates and pilgrims at KCBC
candidates.summary: Bushwick Figure Drawing runs a costumed life-drawing session in the KCBC taproom on Monday Nov 23, 7 to 9pm, with a Mayflower-intercepted-by-pirates theme. All levels, some supplies provided, tickets via their link in bio.
candidates.fit: Brewery plus interactive plus genuinely odd, which is three of his boxes, and he gets to come home with a drawing. Monday, so it's a radar item rather than a headline.

candidates.title: Einstein on the Beach: 50th Anniversary Concert at BAM
candidates.summary: BAM's Next Wave marks fifty years of Philip Glass's Einstein on the Beach with a concert version running Nov 19 to 21, the piece BAM premiered in 1984 and revived in 1992 and 2012. Ticket prices were not in the announcement.
candidates.fit: He left Philip Glass blank, so this is not a lead pick, but it is a once-in-a-decade night three blocks from his door and the email has barely used BAM. Flag it, don't sell it.

candidates.title: Strong Rope 2027 Mug Club sign-ups
candidates.summary: Strong Rope opened 2027 Mug Club sign-ups, which include a free pour every day you visit the taproom plus member brew days, release parties and discounts. Sign-ups run through Dec 1, 2026. Membership price was not stated in the post.
candidates.fit: He already treats a sunny Strong Rope afternoon as a plan; this makes it a standing one, and it's the rare gift idea that isn't a candle. Deadline Dec 1.

laneReports.notes:
Hard limit again: the search and fetch tooling cut out with repeated server tool-use errors roughly two-thirds of the way through this lane, so several planned passes never ran. What is above is honest.

Verified by reading the organizer's own calendar: all four Friends and Lovers items (Y2K night Nov 19, SAZONAO Nov 20, Algo. Riddim Nov 21, Open Jam Nov 25). Friends and Lovers in Crown Heights is a room the email has never used, and its programming is exactly the Caribbean/Afro-Latin/throwback register the lane brief asked for, so it is worth keeping on the weekly check.

Marked likely, not verified: John Summit at Barclays (the venue's own event page text came back in search results confirming Nov 28 and 29 with Cassian, and johnsummitmusic.com lists both dates, but I could not open the page myself); Tyla at Brooklyn Paramount Nov 28 (Songkick, Apple Music and TickPick all agree on Nov 28, 8pm, and Songkick carries a second Nov 29 date; brooklynparamount.com returns url_not_accessible to the fetcher); Brent Faiyaz Dec 3, Kes Dec 19 and R&B Only Live Jan 2 (read off the Songkick venue calendars, which I did open, but not off the venue's own page). Marked unverified: the Sultan Room Afrobeat Nights date, which two listings place on Nov 28 and the Dice slug places on Nov 29 (same party, 11pm doors, just a date-rollover disagreement); both NYE items.

Useful negatives confirmed this week, so nobody re-runs them: Sean Paul has one upcoming concert and it is not in New York; Asake, Omah Lay, Burna Boy and Wizkid have no New York dates (Omah Lay's Prudential Center listing is a past Summer Jam); Tyla is the only headliner from the Afrobeats/amapiano lane with an NYC date in either window. Barclays has nothing else in his lanes through early January besides John Summit and Brent Faiyaz. Bossa Nova Civic Club (a tick) is running free weeknight happy-hour sessions, but every lineup in the window is deep-cut locals, i.e. the filler he complained about, so nothing from there.

Gaps that remain for next week, same as last week plus new ones: Basement NY (site is a JavaScript app, returns nothing to the fetcher; needs site: searches or RA promoter pages), Nowadays (its programming now lives entirely on RA, which renders client-side), The Lot Radio events page, Under the K Bridge, Kings Theatre (blocks the fetcher), MSG calendar (Songkick fetch failed on the tool limit, so no check on Drake/Travis/Ice Spice/Knicks-adjacent arena nights), German and Berlin acts touring NYC (never got searched this week), 2000s New York rap nights and Brooklyn drill, Flatbush/Crown Heights dancehall rooms proper (Bembe, Sip N Chat, Acoustik Garden), Teksupport and Avant Gardner/Mirage status, and Saturday/Sunday daytime parties. Knockdown Center was deliberately skipped per the usual-suspects rule.

Blunt accounting: my server tool budget was cut off again, and this time it died early and hard. Web fetch stopped working after roughly a dozen calls and web search stopped a few calls later, so most of this lane never got researched. Three of my four candidates are honest leads rather than finished picks, and only the Other Half festival is verified.

What I actually read in full: the Resident article on the MŪJE x TIN's dinner (Nov 16, two seatings, chefs named, no price given anywhere on the page); Other Half's homepage, which carries the Stout Season Festival banner with the December 5, 2026 date, the Centre Street location and the Eventbrite link I used; KCBC's full events page; Maccabee Bar's homepage; Strong Rope's homepage; Brooklyn Magazine's homepage; Pioneer Works' Choke Hole page.

Verified negatives, so nobody chases them again: KCBC's events page currently reads 'Nothing coming up' for the taproom, so their bingo/trivia/costume programming is either unlisted or on pause. Choke Hole drag wrestling at Pioneer Works is dated November 2025 and is past; the Eventbrite pages that surface in search are last year's. RAW Wine New York 2026 happened November 8 at Industry City and is past. grubstreet.com returns url_not_allowed to the fetcher, same as last week's report on ny.eater.com, theinfatuation.com, resy.com, exploretock.com and punchdrink.com, and site: queries against Eater returned only Wikipedia noise.

What never got opened and should be the first five fetches next week: (1) strongropebrewery.com/events, (2) otherhalfbrewing.com/event-type/all-locations (their full taproom calendar, which would also give Stout Season ticket prices and any Thanksgiving-week releases), (3) maccabeebar.com/locations-2 for the 2026 New York host bar and opening night, (4) bkmag.com/2026/11/09/where-to-eat-in-brooklyn-this-week and the Nov 11 weekend guide, both of which were on the homepage and are the likeliest source of Brooklyn pop-ups and chef takeovers in this window, (5) threesbrewing.com/events and radegasthall.com, neither of which I could reach.

Still unresearched in this lane: Thanksgiving-eve bar nights and Friendsgiving group dinners for Nov 25-26; whole-animal and banquet dinners; cocktail bar guest shifts and takeovers; mezcal and whiskey nights; Sunken Harbor Club special nights (the site blocks the fetcher, so it needs a search workaround or a look at Gage & Tollner's events page); bar wrestling and bar bingo in Bushwick and Bed-Stuy; and the December holiday pop-up bars beyond Maccabee. Prices are missing on three of four candidates for the same reason, and none of the undated items should be printed as plans until someone confirms them.

Hard constraint: the search and fetch budget was cut off mid-pass, well before this lane was finished. I got organizer-page reads on companyxiv.com (Nutcracker Rouge confirmed as the current show) and stannswarehouse.org (current season: Tristan & Yseult, Saigon, Return of the Buffalo, Kramer/Fauci), plus search-engine renderings of unionhallny.com, brooklyncc.com, thetinycupboard.com, littlefield's Eventbrite and the Bell House's Ticketmaster venue page. Everything else is secondary, and I have marked it that way rather than calling it verified.

What failed or went unchecked: green-wood.org/events returned nothing, so no catacomb concerts or night tours this week. Nitehawk's homepage carried no listings and I never got to the Williamsburg or Prospect Park calendars, so there is no costume or themed screening in this batch — that gap is now two weeks old and should be the first thing covered next pass, along with Alamo Brooklyn and the Rocky Horror shadowcast listing at Berlin on Avenue A that has still never been verified. Also uncovered: BAM, BRIC, Theatre for a New Audience, Irondale, Mark Morris, Roulette, JACK, Pioneer Works Second Sundays, the Slipper Room, House of Yes, Brooklyn Art Haus and Don't Tell Comedy's current secret-location dates.

Two leads worth chasing first next week. One: unionhallny.com lists 'Cold Plunge with Kurt Braunohler' and 'Best Year Ever' as upcoming without dates I could read — Braunohler is a name he would place and the title alone lines up with his sauna-and-plunge interest. Two: the Bell House has Ralph Barbosa on its Ticketmaster artist list with no date visible; a Netflix-special comic in a 300-cap Gowanus bar is exactly the pick this lane is supposed to produce, and it needs one fetch to pin down.

On the ticked-name front: I checked Bill Burr, Nikki Glaser, Stavros Halkias, Jon Stewart, Fred Armisen and Comedy Bang! Bang! for New York dates. None of them has a date inside either window — Armisen's Beacon run and Stavros at Radio City are both past, and Comedy Bang! Bang! is not back until June. So there is no 'name he knows in a room he does not expect' this week, and I would rather say that plainly than dress up an alt-comedy bill as one.

Room-repeat warning: Littlefield has carried three picks already and Union Hall one; both appear here because the week was thin, not because they beat something better. If Nitehawk, the Slipper Room or Green-Wood turn up anything next pass, drop the Littlefield item.

Budget failure, stated plainly: my web tools died roughly a third of the way through this lane. The search tool stopped returning after about 20 queries and the fetch tool then started timing out on every call, so a large part of the planned hunt never happened. Everything above comes from a page I actually read: the Bell House's own calendar (organizer, marked verified), the DOC NYC film page (organizer, verified), and BrooklynVegan's NYC listings pages, which carry the organizer ticket links but which I could not cross-check on Ticketmaster or ATG before the tools cut out (marked likely). No prices are invented; where the page did not show one, the field is empty.

Useful negatives I did confirm before the cutoff, so nobody re-hunts them: Fred Armisen's Comedy For Musicians fall leg ran Oct 3 to Oct 30 and his New York date was the Beacon on Oct 16, already past. deadmau5 has no New York date on Songkick or RA (next listed are LA Jan 9 and Montreal Igloofest Jan 30). Eric Prydz's current run lists Denver Nov 27, Boston Dec 4 and Chicago Dec 5 with no New York date I could find. Paul Kalkbrenner has no US dates. Burna Boy and Wizkid show nothing in New York (Burna Boy's next is Abuja Dec 30). Bill Burr, Nikki Glaser, Stavros Halkias and Jon Stewart all show no New York dates in either window on Ticketmaster or Songkick; Stewart's local date was Stand Up For Heroes on Nov 9, past.

What never got checked and should lead next week: the Comedy Cellar and the Stand drop-in lineups; Joe's Pub, (le) poisson rouge, Littlefield, Caveat, Brooklyn Art Haus and Union Hall calendars for Nov 19-22 and December; the full Town Hall calendar; Greenlight, Books Are Magic, Strand, 92NY, Asia Society, CFR and Columbia's energy center for a speaker in his lanes; Metrograph, Film Forum, BAM Rose, MoMI and Nitehawk for in-person Q&As; Deutsches Haus at NYU and the Goethe-Institut for German names; the Knicks December schedule and whether UFC or a title fight has announced a Garden or Barclays date before Jan 3. Also unresolved: whether Lil' Kim's Nov 19 Kings Theatre night has a legitimate resale route, and the actual showtime and price for the Bell House shows where I only had the venue's list view rather than an event page.

Honest headline: the search and fetch allowance died early this run — roughly fifteen searches and a dozen page fetches in — and it died mid-lane, before I got to most of the Jewish, ideas, creative-scene and family sources. Everything above is either read on a real page or clearly marked unverified. Nothing is invented.

What I actually read. Columbia CGEP's events page loaded in full: the only things on it inside our window are a Nov 17 noon webinar, a Nov 18 9am webinar (AI Data Centers: Is Space the Next Frontier?) and two Nov 18 student roundtables at the center — all virtual or student-only and all weekday daytime, so I left them out rather than pad the lane. There is no in-person CGEP evening event scheduled between now and January 3 on that page. Goethe-Institut New York's site is a navigation shell when fetched; the only in-window item I could confirm is the Azzam talk on Nov 17, which last week's email already sent, plus the exhibition running to Dec 3. Deutsches Haus at NYU still blocks direct fetching (url_not_accessible); their NYU fall-2026 listing page shows only the Dec 2 Malabou lecture in our windows, plus two undated talks (Samuel Weber on Hamann; Robinson/Kovacs on political theater). A third-party NYU page lists a 'Monday, December 2' urbanism panel at Deutsches Haus — Dec 2 2026 is a Wednesday, so that listing is from an earlier year and I excluded it.

What failed or went completely unchecked, in priority order for the next run: German Christmas markets with actual German sponsorship (every result I got was a listicle about Bryant Park and Union Square — skip those, go straight to the German Consulate community calendar, German School Brooklyn, Zum Schneider and the Steuben Society for a Nikolaus or Adventsmarkt); any German-language family event after the Nov 11 Laternenfest; Folksbiene's current production Di Yam Gazlonim (The Pirates of Penzance in Yiddish) at nytf.org/di-yam-gazlonim — real production, dates unread, likely the strongest Jewish-culture pick available if the run covers December; the Maccabee Bar Hanukkah pop-up, which matters because Hanukkah 2026 falls Dec 4–12, squarely in the radar window, and he has loved that bar before; Latke festivals and Jewish deli events; the Jewish Museum, Museum of Jewish Heritage, Center for Jewish History and YIVO calendars (zero coverage this week); 92NY (their events page is JavaScript-only and search gave me nothing dated); CFR, Asia Society, Carnegie Council, Open to Debate and the Economic Club (zero coverage — CFR's public-event feed in particular has resisted two weeks running); the entire creative-scene bucket (open studios, gallery openings that are parties, zine and design fairs) got no searches at all; and on family, NYBG's Holiday Train Show opening date and BBG Lightscape opening date are both unconfirmed even though both are automatic picks in season and he ticked the Train Show himself.

The four family entries are leads, not picks. They are real venues with real URLs and they are the right register, but none has a confirmed date or lineup — do not put a specific Saturday in the email behind any of them without opening the calendar first. If only one can be verified next run, verify Rock and Roll Playhouse: a Beatles or Fleetwood Mac set at 11am with a one-year-old is the single best fit in this lane.

Deliberate omissions: Barbès (carried two picks in the last two issues, and I had no new calendar to read anyway), and the CGEP webinars (virtual, daytime, thin).

Budget: my web_search and web_fetch allowances both ran out early (searches died after about four batches), so most items here rest on the organizer's own Instagram caption, which this lane allows, and are marked likely rather than verified. Only one item is fully verified by reading the organizer page: the Jewish Museum family concert (Nov 22, 11:30am, Scheuer Auditorium, $24 adult, free kids). Prices are blank wherever the caption or listing did not state one; I did not guess any.

What I confirmed by reading search results from ticketing/trade pages but could not fully render: LCD Soundsystem at Music Hall of Williamsburg Nov 17 (AXS listing shows doors 7pm/show 8pm; Pollstar, Paste and Relix all report it as a pop-up and one of the final shows before the venue closes in December; on sale was Mon Nov 16 at 2pm, so it may already be gone by Monday's email). Sting at Brooklyn Paramount: Ticketmaster shows Nov 17 and Nov 21 7pm dates; the venue says four nights remain as of Nov 16, so there are probably two more mid-week dates I could not pin down. Bridget Everett at Joe's Pub Nov 17-20, $85-$135, doors 9pm, two-drink minimum.

Caveats worth printing: LCD Soundsystem and Philip Glass/Einstein on the Beach were both left blank on his checklist; I included them because the room and the occasion are exceptional, not because the names tested well. Murray Hill: Showbiz! at Joe's Pub on Sat Nov 21 looked like a strong drag/variety date-night pick but listings show it sold out, so I left it out. Maccabee Bar's NYC venue and run dates are still unconfirmed, which is the second week running; it is worth one targeted search. Still unverified from last week's gap list and unverified again now: Brooklyn Botanic Garden Lightscape 2026 dates and prices, the Fort Greene Park tree lighting date (Dec 4 vs Dec 5 discrepancy), and NYCB Nutcracker's exact opening date, so I left all three out rather than print a guess.

False leads I filtered: the @kingstheatre posts in the feed are Kings Theatre Portsmouth UK (panto, Shrek), not Flatbush. @lodgeroom, @venturamusichall, @sectionlive and @theludlowgarage posts are out-of-town Rock and Roll Playhouse dates. @bathhouse's anniversary post is a giveaway, and @othership's is too, so both were skipped per the rules. Generic Eventbrite afrobeats promoter nights (Mehanata, Midtown rooftops, 'ladies free before 1am') are the wrong register and were cut. No Muay Thai, kickboxing or car-meet date surfaced in the 425 posts: @daikokunyc appears only via friends' photos with no dated meet, and my search budget died before I could check their ticketing page at tickets.thefoat.com/daikokunyc, which is where their meets are actually sold. That is the biggest gap this week.
